title: The Flowers of Evil, Baudelaire
subject: litterature
description: Baudelaire extracts beauty from evil and everyday Parisian life. Condemned in 1857, the collection founded modern poetry.

hero.hook: Six censored poems, one conviction, and the birth of modern poetry.

blocks.text: In **1857**, **Charles Baudelaire** published **The Flowers of Evil**. The collection marks a turning point in the history of poetry. Until then, **[[Romanticism]]** dominated: poets idealized nature and great feelings. Baudelaire does otherwise. He writes about ugliness, sin, the city, anguish.

The book caused a scandal. He was convicted of “insulting public morals”. However, Baudelaire defends a strong idea: we can draw beauty from what shocks or disgusts. He compares the poet to an alchemist. Where others see only mud, he looks for gold.

**Charles Baudelaire** plays the **cursed poet**: a writer on the fringes, unloved by his time. His difficult life nourishes his work. He loves elegance and refinement, what we call **dandyism**, but he also knows decay and debt.

Orphaned by his father at **6 years**, he quarrels with his father-in-law, General **Aupick**, who controls part of his fortune. He loves **Jeanne Duval**, actress and singer. Their relationship is passionate and conflicted. It inspires several poems in the collection.

blocks.caption: Charles Baudelaire: elegance, pain and modernity.

blocks.text: Six poems were convicted in 1857 and were not officially rehabilitated until 1949, 92 years after the conviction.

In **1857**, the same year as the trial of **[[Madame Bovary]]**, **The Flowers of Evil** also went before the courts. Flaubert and Baudelaire are tried for immorality. Furthermore, Baudelaire translates **Edgar Allan Poe**, American fantasy writer. He considers him a “soul brother”, sharing his taste for the macabre.

The book is not a simple collection of poems. Baudelaire traces a progression there. **“Spleen and Ideal”**, the first major section, opposes two states. **spleen**, a word borrowed from English, designates a deep boredom, a melancholy without cause. The **ideal** is the thirst for elevation and pure beauty.

In **“The Albatross”**, the poet compares himself to this sea bird. In flight, it is majestic. On the deck of the ship, he becomes clumsy and ridiculous. The image sums up the solitude of the misunderstood artist.

blocks.caption: Nocturnal Paris in the 1850s: setting of Baudelairian spleen.

blocks.text: **“Parisian paintings”** makes the city an interior decor. Streets, crowds and passers-by reflect the poet's moods. Under **[[Baron Haussmann]]**, Paris is transformed: wide boulevards, new buildings. Baudelaire then wanders as a **stroller**, that is to say a walker who observes the city without any precise aim. The sections “Wine”, “Flowers of Evil” and “The Revolt” explore escape attempts before the conclusion “Death”.

Baudelaire masters classical forms. He often writes in **sonnet**, a poem of 14 lines, or in **alexandrine**, lines of 12 syllables. But he brings a new vision into it. His poem **“Correspondence”** describes nature as a temple where perfumes, colors and sounds respond to each other.
Nature is a temple where living pillars / Sometimes let out confused words.

Baudelaire develops the idea of ​​**synesthesia**: the senses mix. We can “smell” a color or “see” a perfume. The world becomes a network of signs that the poet must decipher. This poetics opens the way to **[[Symbolism and Baudelaire's legacy]]**, later carried by Verlaine and Mallarmé.
The whole project is summed up in a famous phrase: “You gave me your mud and I made gold from it”. Baudelaire does not deny evil or ugliness. He transforms them into art material.
For Baudelaire, **[[Modernity]]** consists of capturing what passes: urban life, the ephemeral, the everyday. But he also looks for what lasts. The modern poet observes his time without fleeing it.

This attention to the city prepares the **[[Prose poem]]**, poetic text without verse or rhyme. Baudelaire developed it in **[[Le Spleen de Paris]]**, a posthumous collection of short prose poems about Paris.

events.title: Rehabilitation
events.detail: The six censored poems are finally lifted.

blocks.text: Baudelaire also redefines the role of the poet. In Hugo, the poet still guides the nation. In Baudelaire, he becomes a marginal person who sees what society prefers to hide. **The Flowers of Evil** first scandalized, then became a reference for the entire following century.

**The Flowers of Evil** revolutionizes poetry by extracting beauty from evil and everyday urban life. The collection establishes **[[Modernity]]** and **[[Symbolism and Baudelaire's legacy]]**, despite a condemnation which lasted almost a century.
